overview.text: The Common Lancehead (Fer-de-lance) is a highly venomous pit viper of the tropical lowlands of South America east of the Andes and of Trinidad. It causes many snakebites in its range.

size.label: Adults
size.text: Usually 75 to 125 cm long and fairly heavy-bodied.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Colombia, Venezuela, the Guianas, Brazil, eastern Ecuador, Peru, northern Bolivia and Trinidad.

behaviour.text: Mostly lives on the ground and is active at night, but swims well and climbs trees when it needs to. It is easily agitated.

diet.text: Mostly small mammals such as rodents and opossums, and birds, plus frogs, lizards, snakes, fish, crayfish, centipedes and tarantulas. It bites large prey, lets go and follows its scent.

reproduction.text: Gives birth to live young; females can sometimes reproduce without a male.

recognise.text: Heavy pit viper with a lance-shaped head.
